newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended sharply higher, boosted by a recovery in shorter maturities.
The Swiss June Confederate bond futures contract, which will expire June 16, closed up 46 basis points at 121.46.

One EuroSwiss trader on LIFFE said Swiss franc short-term prices may have gained on belief that progress on European Economic and Monetary Union, which includes a plan for a single European currency, is faltering.
The trader said such talk overshadowed fundamentals. He said that in addition there was talk of large stop-loss orders in mark/Swiss at 84.00 centimes.

The mark was below that level after the close of trade here. Swiss franc strength versus the mark is seen as a key factor arguing for lower Swiss rates, after the Swiss National Bank said in May it would aggressively add liqudity to offset Swiss franc gains.

Domestic factors were likely to include Swiss first quarter GDP, expected on Thursday. Swiss economists forecast a rise of 0.3 percent versus the fourth quarter and a drop of 0.4 percent against the first quarter of 1996.
On Wednesday the Swiss National Bank is expected to release its 10-day statement for early June, including sight deposits.
Comi medium-term bond COMIc1 settled down two at 111.83
Euro Swiss francs FESc1 up five at 98.55.
